Yes, water has been found on the Moon, confirmed by multiple missions and analyses. NASA's official Moon Science page reports that the Clementine mission (1994) and Lunar Prospector (1998) found evidence of water ice at the lunar poles, and revisited Apollo samples in 2008 revealed hydrogen in volcanic glass beads indicating ancient lunar water [d1]. The SOFIA mission later confirmed the water molecule H2O in sunlit areas of the Moon for the first time, indicating water is widely distributed across the lunar surface [d3]. The definitive discovery came in 2008 via India's Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft, whose M3 instrument confirmed water ice inside polar craters, and in 2009 NASA's LCROSS probe detected 155 kilograms of water after impacting a south pole crater [d4]. Wikipedia's Lunar water article further notes that Apollo 14 detected water vapor near the lunar surface in 1971, and Soviet Luna 24 samples in 1978 showed approximately 0.1% water by mass [d5]. While the Moon is very dry by Earth standards — the Sahara Desert has 100 times more water than what SOFIA detected — water is present in permanently shadowed polar craters and in sunlit regions [d3][d6].
